column1: Which SQL change feature preserves both the old and new values when a captured column changes?
column2:
Change Data Capture (CDC).
CDC reads the transaction log after changes occur and stores captured values in change tables. For example, an update can preserve both the old and new price.
Review source

column1: What does SQL Change Tracking store so a consumer can find rows that changed without keeping their old values?
column2:
Changed row keys and change metadata.
Change Tracking records enough information to identify rows that changed. Join those keys to the source to read the current values. A deleted key has no source row left to join.
Review source

column1: How can a consumer keep CDC records after the database's retention cleanup removes them?
column2:
Copy changes to a durable archive before cleanup.
Export changes before the retention cleanup removes them. Keep track of the last copied position so a later copy can resume without leaving a gap.
Review source

column1: Which scheduler runs CDC capture and cleanup in SQL Server, and what runs them in Azure SQL Database?
column2:
SQL Server uses Agent jobs. Azure SQL Database uses a built-in scheduler.
For SQL Server, SQL Server Agent normally runs capture and cleanup jobs. Azure SQL Database schedules those tasks internally, so you do not start a separate Agent service.
Review source

column1: How does the Azure Functions SQL trigger detect table changes?
column2:
It polls SQL Change Tracking, not CDC change tables.
The binding periodically checks for changes recorded by Change Tracking. A SQL write can commit before the function even sees it. This is different from a database trigger in the same transaction.
Review source

column1: A row changes from Pending to Paid to Shipped between Functions SQL trigger polls. What can the trigger miss?
column2:
Intermediate changes and their values.
If an order moves from Pending to Paid to Shipped before a poll, the function can see only Shipped. Use a history mechanism when each intermediate transition matters.
Review source

column1: Why can a Functions SQL trigger lose changes if it is offline longer than Change Tracking retention?
column2:
Cleanup can remove changes before the function processes them.
Change Tracking removes records outside its retention window. After a long outage, the function can lose the changes it has not processed. Set retention to cover the expected gap.
Review source

column1: Why enable CDC alongside a Functions SQL trigger when the application must both react to changes and retain old values?
column2:
To retain row-change history while the trigger handles current changes.
Use CDC to retain captured values and the SQL trigger to react to current changes. The trigger does not read the CDC tables. The database platform must support both features.
Review source

column1: Which SQL Server 2025 feature on Windows pushes committed row changes directly to Azure Event Hubs?
column2:
Change event streaming (CES), currently in preview.
CES sends committed row changes to Event Hubs without a consumer polling the source table. It sends asynchronously, so the event does not need to reach Event Hubs before the SQL commit returns.
Review source
Delivery behavior

column1: In SQL Server Change Event Streaming, what does a stream group connect to a destination?
column2:
A configuration that links tracked tables to a streaming destination.
The stream group defines which destination receives changes from its assigned tables. It also defines how the stream authenticates and how it assigns events to partitions.
Review source

column1: Why must CES consumers safely handle the same event more than once?
column2:
CES guarantees at-least-once delivery, so duplicates can occur.
At-least-once delivery means a retry can deliver an event again. Make the action safe to repeat, for example by recording which event you already processed before sending a second notification.
Review source

column1: CES sends SQL changes to Azure Event Hubs. Which Azure Functions trigger reads those events?
column2:
An Event Hubs trigger.
Event Hubs is the function's event source in this pipeline. Use its trigger to consume the stream. The Functions SQL trigger reads Change Tracking from a database instead.
Review source

column1: What information does each SqlChange<T> in a C# SQL trigger batch contain?
column2:
Row data and the operation type.
Item contains the row data in the type you declared. Operation tells the handler which kind of change it is, so it can distinguish a modified row from a deleted row.
Review source

column1: In a Functions SQL trigger, what does ConnectionStringSetting refer to rather than containing the credential itself?
column2:
A function app setting that contains the SQL connection string.
The argument stores the setting name rather than the connection string. Define the named setting in local.settings.json for local testing and in the function app for deployment.
Review source

column1: Which Azure Logic Apps connector provides triggers and actions for Azure SQL Database?
column2:
The SQL Server connector.
The connector appears under the name SQL Server even when it connects to Azure SQL Database. Once connected, the workflow can use SQL actions such as reading rows or calling a procedure.
Review source

column1: Which SQL feature must you enable on a table monitored by a Logic Apps Standard built-in SQL trigger?
column2:
Change Tracking.
Enable Change Tracking at database level first, then on the monitored table. Turning it on for the database alone does not make the table eligible for the trigger.
Review source

column1: What connects a Logic Apps Consumption workflow to an on-premises SQL Server?
column2:
An on-premises data gateway.
The gateway relays connector requests from the cloud workflow to the on-premises SQL Server. The SQL connection uses the gateway rather than expecting the database to have a public endpoint.
Review source

column1: Which column does the Logic Apps managed SQL trigger When an item is created (V2) require?
column2:
An IDENTITY column.
The managed trigger uses increasing IDENTITY values to recognize new rows. An ordinary primary key, such as a GUID, does not satisfy this trigger's requirement.
Review source

column1: Which column does the Logic Apps managed SQL trigger When an item is modified (V2) require?
column2:
A ROWVERSION column.
SQL changes a ROWVERSION value when a row is inserted or updated. The managed trigger uses that marker to detect newer rows. ROWVERSION is not a date or time.
Review source

column1: How does the Logic Apps Consumption trigger When an item is created use its frequency and interval to detect new rows?
column2:
It polls the table on the configured schedule.
The connector checks at the configured frequency and interval, such as every five minutes. It does not receive a push from SQL at insert time, so detection can lag.
Review source
